title: Karma Yoga
hook: a fly lands on a pot of honey to sip, and finds its feet stuck
carry: keep your feet on the rim

segments.voice: Yesterday, Karma Yoga and the moral gymnasium, where the giver is the one who says thank you. Did you get to say it first? Day nine hundred forty-three.

A fly finds a pot of honey. What luck. It lands on the rim, walks down to the sweet part, and starts to drink. A minute later it tries to lift off, and can't. Its feet are stuck in the very thing it came to enjoy. Vivekananda uses a picture like this in his talks on Karma Yoga, and it isn't really about flies. It's about a new job, a relationship, a project, a phone. Today, why the path of work spends so much time on getting unstuck.
screen: `A FLY FINDS HONEY.` → `IT COMES TO SIP.` → `ITS FEET ARE STUCK.`

segments.voice: Vivekananda's diagnosis comes in a run of short reversals. We came to enjoy, and we're being enjoyed. We came to rule, and we're being ruled. We came to work, and we're being worked. The honey isn't the problem. Work isn't the problem either; again and again he tells people to work. The trouble is the sticking: work done for what it will get us, so that the getting owns us. So how do you drink without getting stuck? He's clear that the answer is not to stay away from the honey. Running from the world doesn't free anyone. The answer he calls non-attachment, and he offers two roads to it, for two kinds of people. If you believe in God, there's the road of the Bhagavad Gita: work, and give the results away to God, the way you'd lay a flower at a shrine. The work is yours to do. What comes of it isn't yours to clutch. And if you don't believe in God, he doesn't send you away. He offers the road of reflection and will: keep telling yourself, this outcome is not me, this praise is not me, this failure is not me, until it's true. Notice how practical that is. Listeners who pray and listeners who don't, and he hands each of them something to use on Monday. The fly can still drink. It just learns to keep its feet on the rim.
screen: `WE CAME TO WORK; WE'RE BEING WORKED.` · `DON'T RUN FROM THE HONEY.` · `ROAD ONE: GIVE THE RESULTS TO GOD.` · `ROAD TWO: THIS IS NOT ME.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let the breath settle. Name one thing you're working on right now that you care about a lot. Notice where your feet are stuck: a result you need, a person's approval, a number. Choose whichever road fits you. If you pray, you might picture setting that result down at a shrine, and leaving it there. If you don't, you might say silently on each out-breath: this result is not me. Either way, keep caring about the work. Just lift one foot off the honey. The bell holds the time.
Karma Yoga. The yoga of work: drinking the honey without getting stuck in it.
Your line: keep your feet on the rim. Today, do one task with full care, then let go of how it lands before anyone tells you. Day nine hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: Hindus who follow the Bhagavad Gita's teaching on work describe offering their work to God without clinging to its results, and Vedanta study circles read Vivekananda's Karma Yoga alongside the Gita.

fork.setup: you're the fly, and your feet are stuck in the honey you came to enjoy. what does the yoga of work tell you to do?
options: keep drinking, but learn not to sink your feet in.
fork.reveal: Vivekananda's answer isn't to leave the world. it's non-attachment: do the work fully, and let the results go, by offering them to God or by seeing they aren't you.

original.note: Sanskrit: non-attachment, not being stuck to the results.

trapdoor: what you thought: non-attachment means not caring.
what it means: caring fully about the work, without being owned by what it gets you.
what a scholar hears: Vivekananda offers two roads, the Gita's offering of results to God and, for non-believers, a road of reflection and will.

sources.ref: Swami Vivekananda, Karma-Yoga, the chapters on the secret of work and on non-attachment
sources.work: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, vol. 1 (paraphrased)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Karma-Yoga: the fly-on-honey image ('we came to sip the honey, and found our feet stuck'), and the reversals ('we came to enjoy; we are being enjoyed. we came to rule; we are being ruled. we came to work; we are being worked'); confirm which chapter (the secret of work or non-attachment).
Confirm that the chapter on non-attachment offers two ways, one for those who believe in God (giving up the fruits to the Lord) and one for those who do not (will, reflection, 'neti neti').
Gita 5.10 (offering actions to Brahman, like a lotus leaf untouched by water) is cited for the offering road; confirm the verse choice.
Original: अनासक्ति; confirm. Year-one days covered 'work like a master, not a slave', so that image is left out here.

Editor pass: softened 'he spends the whole book telling people to work hard' to 'again and again he tells people to work', and made the 'whole room' line name the two kinds of listener the two roads serve.
